The measured loss is about $\approx 0.14$ per cycle, and the sample needs at least
$\geq 2$ trials before the estimate settles. The yield was $\geq 90\%$ in every run.

A response rate of 95\% was reported in 2024 for 12 participants, with a mean age of 34.5 years
and a dose of 5 mg per kilogram [3]. See Figure 3 and Table 2 on page 7 (Section 4.1).

\begin{enumerate}
\item The first step takes 10 minutes.
\item The second step takes 25\% longer than the first.
\end{enumerate}
